newsitem.title: USA: Lockheed's WorldCom suit on hold.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed's WorldCom suit on hold.

text.p: A Delaware judge Tuesday issued a standstill order on Lockheed Martin Corp's lawsuit seeking to overturn a $500 million contract for electronic toll collection awarded to WorldCom Inc unit MFS Technologies Inc.

In a two page decision, Vice Chancellor Bernard Balick of the Delaware Chancery Court said he would stay discovery on Lockheed's motions for a preliminary injunction blocking the contract from going forward and for expedited proceedings.
Balick also asked the defendants, MFS and the Delaware Department of Transportation, to brief him on their motion seeking dismissal of the case based on the court's alleged lack of jurisdiction.
Delaware deputy attorney general Frederick Schranck told Reuters Lockheed allegedly has no legal basis for its lawsuit.

"Lockheed is saying that Delaware should have followed its own bid laws. But we asked the Budget Commission of the Delaware General Assembly if we could piggyback on the New Jersey contract and the Commission approved of that," Schranck said.

According to Schranck, Delaware's share of the contract for converting the state's manual toll collection to an electronic system would be about $11 million. The bulk of the contract would be for converting New Jersey toll collection to an electronic system.
A hearing before the New Jersey Transit Authority hearing officer is set to begin April 14 on Lockheed's administrative appeal there from the bid, Schranck said.
